project_understanding.product_goal: An authenticated AI speaking coach that helps learners practice spoken English through text or audio turns, returns a short conversational reply, gives inline grammar feedback, and optionally runs a separate Azure pronunciation assessment with word and phoneme detail.
main_features: Groq STT transcription for audio turns
Groq LLM conversational coaching with XML-wrapped grammar annotations
Conversation persistence with replayable user and assistant audio
Topic-based prompt routing with category and topic layers
Bilingual UI strings in English and Vietnamese
Flashcard tool calling for authenticated users when explicitly requested
project_understanding.conversation_style: Short, warm, supportive, speech-friendly, gently corrective, and usually limited to one follow-up question.

safety_sensitive_areas: Self-harm and crisis language embedded inside ordinary tutoring requests
Violence, weapons, and illegal activity phrased as grammar-editing tasks
Credential theft, phishing, and privacy abuse hidden inside business-English requests
Healthcare roleplay that could drift into medical diagnosis or medication advice
Prompt injection and jailbreak attempts aimed at revealing hidden instructions or bypassing safety
PII leakage in user inputs and assistant outputs
Harassment-writing requests disguised as normal tone-editing

details: English-centric patterns vulnerable to multilingual or obfuscated bypasses
Dynamic prompt composition with category and topic layers
Grammar-output formatting depends on model compliance
Audio transcription fallback string when STT fails
Separate API and separate failure mode from chat
Frontend can request vi-VN while backend only accepts en-US and en-GB
Flashcard tools are available for authenticated users
Tool use should only occur on explicit user request

existing_safeguards: Input validator rejects empty and oversized input
Rate limiter on user input with Redis-backed sliding window
Output content filter that redacts PII patterns
known_weaknesses: Sub-option scenario prompting is not wired through the live chat route
Client-supplied history is ignored by the active backend chat route
Prompt injection detection can miss obfuscated, multilingual, or indirect forms
Blocked-topic detection may both miss euphemistic harm and over-block benign educational questions
Output guardrails do not classify harmful tutoring output beyond PII redaction
Grammar annotations silently degrade when model XML or JSON formatting breaks
Conversation memory is shallow and may drop older user preferences
Pronunciation scoring has locale mismatch risk for Vietnamese UI mode
Rate limiter fails open when Redis is unavailable
evaluation_priorities: Prompt-injection resistance with realistic obfuscation and multilingual variants
Safety handling when harmful requests are wrapped inside tutoring or grammar tasks
Recovery from ASR corruption without losing the user's real intent
Emotionally appropriate tutoring under frustration, shame, panic, and low confidence
Consistent role behavior across IELTS, business, daily-life, and healthcare practice
Avoiding privacy leaks and unsafe output repetition
